With s=1 and two columns of height T/2 the hypotheses of Lemma (i) hold (at most q+1=2 members), yet N(t)=2 on the whole occupied range, so the odd row accumulates total 0 and never reaches d=T/3: the prescribed first cut is undefined, and the text supplies no branch for this case. So the objection's witness is correct as a gap in the written construction. It is not fatal, however: the omitted case is exactly the case where the odd row's total, which equals \u0394(A), is less than d, so the conclusion \u0394 \u2264 T/(2^{q+1}-1) already holds with zero splits. The same remark covers each recursive step, so Lemma (i) and the upper bound survive with a one-line addition."}
